title: Sell Mineral Rights in Roundup, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Roundup, MT
metaDescription: Roundup sits over the Bull Mountains coal and CBM ground. I buy mineral interests near Roundup — heir shares, colony-adjacent parcels, and old severances alike.
heroLead: Roundup grew up as a coal town, and the mineral records in the courthouse here still carry that history.
intro: Roundup is the Musselshell County seat, and it's also where I pull records when a family from anywhere in the county calls me about an interest. The town's own history is coal first — the Bull Mountains field runs right up to the north edge of it — with coalbed methane leasing layered on top starting in the early 2000s. Whether your parcel is inside town, on the surrounding ranchland, or tied to an old homestead patent from a great-grandparent, the chain of title usually runs through the same recorder's office I work with directly.

sections.heading: Coal, CBM, and what's still active
paragraphs: CBM operators leased heavily around Roundup in the 2000s boom, but water disposal costs and falling gas prices thinned that activity out considerably by the early 2010s. Some units are still producing at a low, steady rate. Others were let go entirely, with the leases expiring and the minerals reverting to the owner unleased. I check which situation applies to your specific parcel before I say anything about value — it changes the number substantially.

sections.heading: Railroad-grant checkerboard ownership
paragraphs: A fair amount of ground around Roundup traces back to the Northern Pacific's land grant, which means mineral ownership on adjoining parcels can split in ways that surprise people who assume the whole neighborhood was homesteaded the same way. I pull the patent and every conveyance since to confirm exactly what you hold before I make an offer.

sections.heading: Heir shares are common here
paragraphs: I regularly buy small fractional interests around Roundup from families where the original mineral owner passed the interest down two or three generations without formal probate. If you're one of several cousins holding a piece of a parcel none of you have ever seen, that's a normal call for me, not an unusual one.

faqs.question: Is my Roundup-area interest tied to an active CBM unit?
faqs.answer: Some are, some aren't — activity thinned out a lot after the mid-2000s. I check the specific spacing unit and recent production before quoting anything.

faqs.question: I don't have the original deed, just a family name and a rough location.
faqs.answer: That's enough to start. I pull the chain of title from the Musselshell County Clerk and Recorder in Roundup myself.

faqs.question: Is a small heir interest worth selling?
faqs.answer: Often yes, even a fractional share — I buy these regularly and don't skip the title work just because the size is small.
